ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A square piece of paper has sides of length $ 100$. From each corner a wedge is cut in the following manner: at each corner, the two cuts for the wedge each start at distance $ \sqrt{17}$ from the corner, and they meet on the diagonal at an angle of $ 60^\circ$ (see the figure below). The paper is then folded up along the lines joining the vertices of adjacent cuts. When the two edges of a cut meet, they are taped together. The result is a paper tray whose sides are not at right angles to the base. The height of the tray, that is, the perpendicular distance between the plane of the base and the plane formed by the upper edges, can be written in the form $ \sqrt{n}{m}$, where $ m$ and $ n$ are positive integers, $ m < 1000$, and $ m$ is not divisible by the $ n$th power of any prime. Find $ m + n$.

The two tangent lines labeled cut start respectively from these starting points on the two sides and intersect at the same point on the diagonal of the corner; in the figure, the diagonal divides the cut angle into 30° and 30°, so the angle between the two cut lines is 60°. From this intersection point, a horizontal fold line and a vertical fold line are also drawn, representing the fold line formed by connecting adjacent cut vertices. Reasoning: Let s=√17, take the corner point as the origin, and let the cut starting points on the two sides be A=(0,s), B=(s,0). The cut intersection point lies on the diagonal, suppose it is P=(a,a). Since in the figure the diagonal bisects 60°, this is equivalent to ∠APB=60°. From the symmetric angle condition, one can obtain a/s=(1+√3)/2. After cutting off the corner wedge, near P take the two adjacent fold lines as mutually perpendicular coordinate axes in the base plane; the lower side face is folded upward around one axis by angle θ, and the left side face is folded upward around the other perpendicular axis by the same angle θ. Rotate A and B respectively with their own side faces. Since the two sides of the cut are pasted together, the rotated positions of A and B must coincide, therefore obtaining cosθ=(a-s)/a. The tray height is the vertical component after folding upward of a point whose distance from the fold axis is a, namely h=a sinθ. So h²=a²-(a-s)²=s²(2a/s-1). Substituting s²=17 and 2a/s-1=√3 gives h²=17√3, hence h⁴=867. Thus h=the fourth root of 867, namely h=√[4]{867}, so m=867, n=4, and m+n=871.

method.method_draft: Use a distance-to-fold-axis solid-geometry method, avoiding explicit rotation formulas. First read the image locally: at a corner, the two cut endpoints are s=sqrt(17) from the corner on perpendicular sides, and the cut lines meet at P on the diagonal with 30 degrees on each side, so the two cut lengths are symmetric. Place P as the base corner after folding, with the two fold lines as perpendicular axes in the base plane. From the flat diagram, if P=(a,a) relative to the original corner, then the foot of the perpendicular from a cut endpoint to its fold line is offset by a-s along the fold line, and the perpendicular distance from that endpoint to the fold line is a. Determine a from the flat 60-degree wedge condition: with endpoints (0,s) and (s,0) and P=(a,a), the angle APB is 60 degrees, yielding a/s=(1+sqrt(3))/2. In the folded tray, the taped endpoint C of the two cut edges has the same perpendicular distance a from each of the two fold axes, while its horizontal projection along each fold axis is fixed by the flat offset a-s. Thus the right triangle from C to either fold axis has hypotenuse a, horizontal leg a-s, and vertical leg h. Therefore h^2=a^2-(a-s)^2=17sqrt(3). Squaring again gives h^4=867, so the height is the fourth root of 867. Hence m+n=867+4=871.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中展示了正方形纸的一个角。原角在左下，沿左边和下边各标出距离 √17；两条标为 cut 的剪线分别从这两个端点出发并相交于右上方的点 P。原角到 P 的线是角平分方向，图中在 P 处标出 30° 和 30°，所以两条剪线夹角为 60°。从 P 向上和向右分别有标为 fold 的折线，互相垂直。
推理：令 s = √17，把原角放在 O=(0,0)，两个剪线起点为 A=(0,s), B=(s,0)。由于 P 在对角线上，设 P=(a,a)。由 ∠APB=60°，向量 PA=(-a,s-a), PB=(s-a,-a)。它们长度相等，且点积为 2a(a-s)。所以 cos60° = 2a(a-s)/(a^2+(a-s)^2)=1/2，即 4a(a-s)=a^2+(a-s)^2。令 r=a/s，得到 4r(r-1)=r^2+(r-1)^2，化简为 2r^2-2r-1=0，因此 r=(1+√3)/2，故 a=s(1+√3)/2。
折叠后，以 P 为底面角，两条 fold 线成为底面内互相垂直的轴。对一个剪线端点来说，它到对应折轴的空间距离保持为平面中到折线的距离 a；同时它在折轴方向上的偏移量保持为 a-s。两条剪边粘合后的同一点 C 到任一折轴形成直角三角形：斜边为 a，底面水平腿为 a-s，竖直腿为托盘高度 h。因此 h^2=a^2-(a-s)^2=(a-(a-s))(a+(a-s))=s(2a-s)。代入 a=s(1+√3)/2，得 2a-s=s√3，所以 h^2=s^2√3=17√3。于是 h^4=17^2·3=867，故 h=四次根号867。题目形式中 n=4, m=867，所以 m+n=871。

折叠后，以 P 为底面角，两条 fold 线成为底面内互相垂直的轴。对一个剪线端点来说，它到对应折轴的空间距离保持为平面中到折线的距离 a；同时它在折轴方向上的偏移量保持为 a-s。两条剪边粘合后的同一点 C 到任一折轴形成直角三角形：斜边为 a，底面水平腿为 a-s，竖直腿为托盘高度 h。因此 h^2=a^2-(a-s)^2=(a-(a-s))(a+(a-s))=s(2a-s)。代入 a=s(1+√3)/2，得 2a-s=s√3，所以 h^2=s^2√3=17√3。于是 h^4=17^2·3=867，故 h=四次根号867。题目形式中 n=4, m=867，所以 m+n=871。

raw_record.original_question: A square piece of paper has sides of length $100$. From each corner a wedge is cut in the following manner: at each corner, the two cuts for the wedge each start at distance $\sqrt{17}$ from the corner, and they meet on the diagonal at an angle of $60^\circ$ (see the figure below). The paper is then folded up along the lines joining the vertices of adjacent cuts. When the two edges of a cut meet, they are taped together. The result is a paper tray whose sides are not at right angles to the base. The height of the tray, that is, the perpendicular distance between the plane of the base and the plane formed by the upper edges, can be written in the form $\sqrt{n}{m}$, where $m$ and $n$ are positive integers, $m < 1000$, and $m$ is not divisible by the $n$th power of any prime. Find $m + n$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows one corner of a square sheet of paper, with the corner point at the lower left, and the two sides perpendicular to each other; along the left side and the bottom side, the distances from the corner point to the starting points of the cuts are each marked as √17. The two tangent lines labeled cut start respectively from these starting points on the two sides and intersect at the same point on the diagonal of the corner; in the figure, the diagonal divides the cut angle into 30° and 30°, so the angle between the two cut lines is 60°. From this intersection point, a horizontal fold line and a vertical fold line are also drawn, representing the fold line formed by connecting adjacent cut vertices. Reasoning: Let s=√17, take the corner point as the origin, and let the cut starting points on the two sides be A=(0,s), B=(s,0). The cut intersection point lies on the diagonal, suppose it is P=(a,a). Since in the figure the diagonal bisects 60°, this is equivalent to ∠APB=60°. From the symmetric angle condition, one can obtain a/s=(1+√3)/2. After cutting off the corner wedge, near P take the two adjacent fold lines as mutually perpendicular coordinate axes in the base plane; the lower side face is folded upward around one axis by angle θ, and the left side face is folded upward around the other perpendicular axis by the same angle θ. Rotate A and B respectively with their own side faces. Since the two sides of the cut are pasted together, the rotated positions of A and B must coincide, therefore obtaining cosθ=(a-s)/a. The tray height is the vertical component after folding upward of a point whose distance from the fold axis is a, namely h=a sinθ. So h²=a²-(a-s)²=s²(2a/s-1). Substituting s²=17 and 2a/s-1=√3 gives h²=17√3, hence h⁴=867. Thus h=the fourth root of 867, namely h=√[4]{867}, so m=867, n=4, and m+n=871.
